**Allowed origins** are set by the `cors({ origin: (origin) => … })` middleware in `worker/src/index.ts:19-35`. It echoes back the request's origin if one of these is true:
- It equals `http://localhost:4200` exactly.
- It ends with `.pages.dev`.
- It ends with `.workers.dev`.

Anything else gets `null`, as does a request with no `Origin` header, so the browser blocks it. Allowed methods are `GET`, `POST`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` and `OPTIONS`. Allowed headers are `Content-Type` and `Authorization`. `maxAge` is 86400.

**To add a custom domain**, edit the `if (...)` condition at `worker/src/index.ts:23-27`. Add one more `||` clause inside it:
- For one exact origin, use `origin === 'https://play.example.com'`. Include the scheme and no trailing slash.
- For all subdomains, use `origin.endsWith('.example.com')`.

Don't add it to an array. The code comment at line 20 and `worker/src/index.md:24` both say Hono matches array entries as exact strings, which is why this is a function. After the edit, redeploy the Worker.

`endsWith('.pages.dev')` also matches `https://evil.pages.dev`, so any Pages site can call the API. Keep that in mind when you widen the rule. I haven't read `docs/DEPLOYMENT_NOTES.md` §4 (CORS), which `index.md` points to for more detail.
